s1.syndrome_frame: Painless, firm, indurated lesion with erythema and granulomatous inflammation in the periocular region
salient_findings: Painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema below the left lower eyelid
Focal, non-tender, indurated elevation along the inferior orbital rim
Granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and multinucleated giant cells on histopathology
key_facts: 69-year-old woman
Several-month history of the lesion
History of chronic scleritis treated with NSAIDs
Left levator resection for ptosis
Dacryocystorhinostomy one month before the onset of the lesion
Two courses of antibiotics for presumed postoperative cellulitis
Lesion persisted despite antibiotic treatment
CT scan showed soft-tissue thickening of the anterior-inferior orbital rim and lower eyelid
No bony invasion or extension into surrounding structures
Excisional biopsy performed
Intraoperative frozen sections revealed granulomatous inflammation
Final histopathology showed granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and multinucleated giant cells
No evidence of malignancy
Bacterial and fungal stains (Ziehl–Neelsen and Grocott) were negative

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and multinucleated giant cells

shortlist.label: Granuloma faciale
shortlist.why_kept: Painless, firm, indurated lesion with erythema and granulomatous inflammation in the periocular region

shortlist.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and soft-tissue thickening of the anterior-inferior orbital rim and lower eyelid

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and negative bacterial and fungal stains

shortlist.label: Periocular granuloma annulare
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and indurated elevation along the inferior orbital rim

raw.rationale: The presence of granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and multinucleated giant cells, along with Alcian-Blue positive mucin, is more consistent with necrobiotic xanthogranuloma than a simple chalazion.

rejected.label: Chalazion
rejected.why: Lack of typical lipid-laden macrophages and the presence of necrobiosis and multinucleated giant cells

rejected.label: Granuloma faciale
rejected.why: Typically presents with brownish plaques on the face and lacks the characteristic necrobiosis of necrobiotic xanthogranuloma

rejected.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
rejected.why: Usually presents with more acute inflammation and does not typically show necrobiosis or multinucleated giant cells

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Would typically show non-caseating granulomas without necrobiosis and often involves other organs

rejected.label: Periocular granuloma annulare
rejected.why: Typically presents with palisading granulomas and lacks the necrobiosis seen in necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
